'''Christopher J. Chang''' is an American chemist and the Edward and Virginia Taylor Professor of Bioorganic Chemistry at [[Princeton University]]. Previously, he was a professor of chemistry and of molecular and cell biology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he holds the Class of 1942 Chair.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Christopher J. Chang|publisher=College of Chemistry, University of California, Berkeley|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/chris-chang|access-date=May 29, 2021}}</ref> Chang is also a member of the [[Helen Wills Neuroscience Institute]], a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] investigator, adjunct professor of [[pharmaceutical chemistry]] at the [[University of California, San Francisco]], and faculty scientist at the chemical sciences division of [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley Lab]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Christopher J. Chang – Chemical Sciences Division Chemical Sciences Division|url=https://commons.lbl.gov/display/csd/Christopher+J.+Chang|access-date=May 29, 2021|website=commons.lbl.gov}}</ref> He is the recipient of several awards for his research in [[bioinorganic chemistry]], molecular and chemical biology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/cjcgrp/ |title=Chang Group – Homepage |publisher=Cchem.berkeley.edu |date= |accessdate=May 6, 2015}}</ref>

His research interests include [[molecular imaging]] sensors for the study of redox biology<ref>{{cite journal|title=Molecular imaging of hydrogen peroxide produced for cell signaling : Abstract : Nature Chemical Biology |journal=Nature Chemical Biology |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=263–267 |doi=10.1038/nchembio871 |pmid= 17401379|year=2007 |last1=Miller |first1=Evan W. |last2=Tulyathan |first2=Orapim |last3=Isacoff |first3=Ehud Y. |last4=Chang |first4=Christopher J. }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=A Targetable Fluorescent Probe for Imaging Hydrogen Peroxide in the Mitochondria of Living Cells |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=130 |issue=30 |pages=9638–9639 |doi=10.1021/ja802355u |pmid=18605728 |pmc=2810491 |year = 2008|last1 = Dickinson|first1 = Bryan C.|last2=Chang |first2=Christopher J. }}</ref> and metals,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Visualizing Ascorbate-Triggered Release of Labile Copper within Living Cells using a Ratiometric Fluorescent Sensor |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=132 |issue=4 |pages=1194–1195 |doi=10.1021/ja907778b |pmid=20052977 |pmc=2819030 |year = 2010|last1 = Domaille|first1 = Dylan W.|last2=Zeng |first2=Li |last3=Chang |first3=Christopher J. }}</ref> especially as applied to [[neuroscience]] and immunology, metal catalysts for renewable energy cycles, and green chemistry.<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Chang was born in 1974 in [[Ames, Iowa]], and was raised in [[Indiana]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Christopher Chang|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/acs-webinars/presenters/chang-christopher.html|access-date=May 29, 2021|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref> He attended the [[California Institute of Technology]] for his undergraduate degree, where he studied chemistry. At Caltech, he worked with [[Harry B. Gray]] on the synthesis and characterization of [[metal salen complexes]] of manganese and vanadium, and nitrogen and oxygen transfer reactivity with these complexes, respectively.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chang|first1=Christopher J.|last2=Low|first2=Donald W.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=1997|title=Reversible Nitrogen Atom Transfer between Nitridomanganese(V) and Manganese(III) Schiff-Base Complexes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ic961023a|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=36|issue=3|pages=270–271|doi=10.1021/ic961023a|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chang|first1=Christopher J.|last2=Connick|first2=William B.|last3=Low|first3=Donald W.|last4=Day|first4=Michael W.|last5=Gray|first5=Harry B.|date=1998|title=Electronic Structures of Nitridomanganese(V) Complexes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ic970598k|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=37|issue=12|pages=3107–3110|doi=10.1021/ic970598k|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chang|first1=Christopher J.|last2=Labinger|first2=Jay A.|last3=Gray|first3=Harry B.|date=December 1, 1997|title=Aerobic Epoxidation of Olefins Catalyzed by Electronegative Vanadyl Salen Complexes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ic970824q|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=36|issue=25|pages=5927–5930|doi=10.1021/ic970824q|pmid=11670216 |issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Chang earned his BS and MS in chemistry in 1997, after which he worked in the laboratory of [[Jean-Pierre Sauvage]] at the [[Université Louis Pasteur]] as a [[Fulbright fellow|Fulbright Fellow]]. In 1999, he moved to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology as a NSF/Merck Graduate Fellow. During his doctoral studies, Chang worked in the laboratory of [[Daniel G. Nocera]]. After earning his PhD in inorganic chemistry in 2002, Chang remained at MIT, working with [[Stephen J. Lippard]] as a Jane Coffin Childs Fellow.

== Independent career ==
In 2004, Chang began his independent career as an assistant professor of chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He was promoted to associate professor in 2009, and full professor of chemistry in 2012, when he was also appointed professor of molecular and cell biology and co-director, chemical biology graduate program.<ref name=":0" /> In 2024, he joined the faculty at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christopher Chang Joins Princeton Chemistry – Princeton University Department of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.princeton.edu/news/christopher-chang-joins-princeton-chemistry/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=chemistry.princeton.edu}}</ref>
